baslik: How Earthquakes Turn Solid Ground to Liquid
aciklama:
In some earthquakes, solid ground turns to liquid and swallows buildings whole. Here is the eerie science.

#shorts #science #earthquake #geology #howitworks

sahneler.metin: In some earthquakes, solid ground turns to liquid.
It sounds impossible, but it swallows entire buildings.
The secret is wet, sandy soil full of water.
Normally the sand grains press together and hold firm.
But violent shaking makes them float apart in the water.
Suddenly the ground acts like a thick liquid, not a solid.
Heavy buildings sink; buried pipes float to the surface.
This is called liquefaction, and it needs no fault line nearby.
The ground you trust is only solid until it is shaken.
